The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 135-136. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Fix J, kh, ah as above. Fix admissible parameters for the small-activity maps of Proposition 8.3, including their block factor L, activity weights A, and analytic radius h0, with the regulator choices allowed by Lemma 9.2. For every ϵ > 0 there are a fixed dyadic integer q, an arbitrarily large dyadic R, P = R5, a dyadic s, and a neighborhood U ⊂ (0, ∞) × int I of (kh, ah), such that the following assertions hold at m = qRs. 135 On the plane there are real, even, square-covariant local activities Km(X; k, a′), invariant under translations of the block grids and under common field translation by 2π/α, with ∥Km(k, a′ )∥m,A,V ≤ ϵ ((k, a′ ) ∈ U). (9.4) Their subset expansion on every dyadic torus fitting the hierarchy and with side n ≥ sP is an exact representation of Equation (9.2), after integrating the observation noise and the Gaussian covariance below side m, up to a field-independent factor that cancels upon normalization. The torus activities obey the same estimate. A support whose padded neighborhood unwraps has exactly its plane activity. This copying property persists under the local maps up to their specified stopping scale. Here fitting means that n/s is a multiple of qR, the torus uses the same grid origin, and n/(mLj) is an integer for every retained coarse grid. On a smaller neighborhood the activities are analytic in k at fixed a′. For every integer r ≥ 0 there is Cr < ∞ such that ∥∂r kKm(k, a′ )∥m,A,V ≤ Crϵ. (9.5) The constants may depend on s, R, J, kh and the chosen neighborhoods. Finite-support evaluations, their field derivatives, and scalar localization projections are continuous in a′. The choices are made in the following order: the downstream norm parameters and the imaginary field strip widths are fixed first; then R and P; then a finite large-field threshold; then s; and finally U. No uniform scaling assertion at temperatures other than kh is part of either the hypotheses or the proof.
